title: Four named HTML elements need explicit ownership
finding: The supplied family architecture did not explicitly account for canvas, picture, source and selectedcontent. All four appear in the captured conforming HTML element index.
decision: Assign canvas to CH-33, picture to CH-29, source jointly to CH-29/CH-30, and selectedcontent to CH-39; include all in APP-A.

title: Move param out of modern embedding instruction
finding: param is in the normative nonconforming obsolete element list, not the conforming element index.
decision: Cover param in APP-F with contextual migration guidance. Explain object without treating param as a current authoring option.

title: Keep element names, integration vocabularies and custom-element rules distinct
finding: 111 physical element-index rows expand to 113 named built-in HTML elements plus svg, math and the autonomous-custom-element category. The h1-h6 group expands to six names.
decision: Retain the physical rows for reconciliation; maintain separate named-HTML and integration records. Give autonomous custom elements an explicit CH-46/APP-A owner. Do not claim 111 or 116 named built-in HTML elements.

title: A single attribute-name list is not an attribute audit
finding: The ordinary attribute index has 180 contextual rows but 144 unique names. Attribute semantics and permitted values vary by element and input state.
decision: Preserve contextual rows, all linked definition targets and separate applicability contexts. Review defaults, state restrictions, reflection and value registries before completing coverage.

title: Correct three discovered index-link mismatches in our reference routing
finding: In the captured informative index, headingoffset and headingreset have applicability links targeting tabindex; slot targets the id definition. The normative global section/definitions provide the appropriate separate targets.
decision: Keep the observed links as evidence and use the extracted global-section definition links in our reference. Do not mistake intentionally specialized title or bdo/dir links for errors.

title: Newer features require independent compatibility treatment
finding: The snapshot includes selectedcontent, headingoffset/headingreset, command/commandfor, closedby, color alpha/colorspace and newer shadowroot attributes. Standard presence alone does not establish broad availability.
decision: Use separate conformance, compatibility and publication-review fields. Six targeted BCD metadata records are captured; browser runtime checks and remaining feature reviews are still pending.

title: Reconcile MDN without treating it as the HTML normative boundary
finding: MDN's captured element tables list 139 names: all 113 conforming HTML names, two foreign-vocabulary roots, 19 matches to the captured obsolete list, and five secondary-only names: geolocation, content, fencedframe, image and shadow.
decision: Keep secondary-only entries in a separate discovery ledger. geolocation's captured BCD source links a WICG proposal, not the WHATWG HTML definition. Historical aliases and external proposals need their own authority/status review.

title: The Standard is larger than an element-and-attribute reference
finding: The full contents snapshot has 17 numbered top-level areas, including separate workers, worklets, storage, communication, processing, rendering and IANA material. Named interfaces alone do not inventory members or algorithms.
decision: Add proposed APP-I for API/interface coverage and explicit depth boundaries. Retain every detailed contents entry with a provisional routing owner. Resolve the depth promise before claiming whole-Standard completeness.

title: Microsyntax and keyword registries need their own audit
finding: The current extraction does not enumerate all rel values, meta names, autocomplete tokens, script-type/import-map rules, sandbox flags, encodings and enumerated attribute states/defaults.
decision: Add proposed APP-J and build definition-level value registries. The captured headers/MIME index is a starting list, not the full HTTP/IANA registry.

title: Accessibility authority and mappings are not yet reconciled
finding: HTML's global section refers to ARIA annotations but does not replace an inventory of allowed roles/properties, accessible names or accessibility mappings. These external documents have not been audited in this foundation.
decision: Reconcile WCAG 2.2, WAI guidance, ARIA in HTML, WAI-ARIA, HTML-AAM and AccName; connect the resulting records to each relevant chapter. Keep this gate explicitly open.

title: Global attributes include ownership and serialization boundaries
finding: The brief global list has 28 HTML-listed names; DOM-owned id, class and slot bring the explicit named set here to 31. data-*, ARIA, CSS Shadow Parts and XML-related allowances are not all the same kind of global attribute.
decision: Keep eight separate family/integration records. Review part/exportparts under CSS Shadow Parts and preserve HTML-versus-XML conditions; do not describe wildcard families as unrestricted attributes.

title: Input applicability and categories contain conditional information
finding: The input summary has 48 physical rows: three group headings and 45 data rows. Its 15 grouped columns represent 22 input states. The content-category index has 15 rows including form-related subcategories and exceptions.
decision: Preserve grouped state membership, source cell text/classes and footnote links; do not flatten every Yes into unconditional permission. Review conditional category memberships and transparent content models per element.

title: Obsolete features have more than one authoring status
finding: The normative snapshot yields 29 obsolete/nonconforming element names, 143 obsolete attribute contexts and seven obsolete-but-conforming conditional paragraphs. These are not one interchangeable deprecated list.
decision: Preserve warning-only conditions separately from prohibited authoring features, including exceptions on script attributes. Keep implementation parsing support distinct from authoring permission.

title: Main event and interface indexes have explicit coverage limits
finding: The main event index omits media-element and drag-and-drop event lists. The all-interfaces list is a named-interface discovery list, not all dictionaries, callbacks, typedefs, members or processing behavior.
decision: Keep 49 main-event rows and 166 named-interface entries with boundary labels. Add missing event inventories and a complete agreed-depth IDL inventory before closing API coverage.

title: Planning artifacts cannot satisfy the campaign promise
finding: No chapter, worked exercise, capstone reference implementation or teaching-example test suite has been produced at this milestone. All feature coverage remains planned.
decision: Use this pack internally. Approve scope and complete the technical inventories before Chapter 1. Do not publish a comment-HTML offer for a complete playbook until the promised deliverable and delivery flow have been tested.

title: Reproducible snapshots are not a pinned upstream release
finding: Captured sources have retrieval metadata and SHA-256 hashes. Live HTML and raw BCD main URLs can change; no upstream revision/commit is pinned for a publication release.
decision: Rebuild this edition from the stored snapshots. At release freeze, pin upstream revisions, review diffs, retain attribution/license notices and record actual reviewer approvals and test environments.
